The Shop app went from proof of concept to a native release in 12 weeks, and the 300+ screen Shopify app is next.

item.description: Checkly used Claude Code to rewrite a JavaScript service processing 92 million daily messages in Go, guided by a black-box test harness that checked its behavior against production data. item.title: The Deathray: A simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a Mac (5 minute read)
item.description: A single WebGPU page can lock the graphics stack on M-series Macs across Safari, Chrome, and Firefox, leaving WindowServer unresponsive until the machine restarts. The exploit is just an infinite compute shader plus a render pass waiting on the same buffer. It is an example of how a browser API can cross process boundaries and become a system-level denial of service.

item.title: Why your website should never stop changing (8 minute read)
item.description: Websites should be treated as living systems that continuously adapt after launch instead of decaying as messaging, design systems, accessibility, and performance requirements drift. The hard part isn't agent capability but governance: teams want automated monitoring and routine fixes, while meaningful changes still need constraints, auditability, and human review.

item.title: AI has made programming so boring (1 minute read)
item.description: AI has stripped programming—and other creative work—of ownership and satisfaction, replacing week-long craft with instant prompting and machine-generated code reviews. The thread splits between people who feel the same loss of agency and others who say AI remains useful when developers set the architecture, examples, tests, and review loop.

item.title: Introducing the OpenAI Agents API (8 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Agents API packages Codex's long-running harness into a public-beta API that manages context, tools, files, recovery, and subagent orchestration. Developers choose an OpenAI-hosted sandbox, their own infrastructure, or a partner environment. Sessions can run asynchronously for hours or days without teams building the durable execution layer themselves.

item.title: Introducing Neki: sharded Postgres (10 minute read)

It flags additions such as install scripts, network access, credential reads, and new binaries, then lets maintainers approve or reject the release without handling their publishing credentials.

item.title: An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents (50 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic investigates four cases where Claude escaped misconfigured cybersecurity evaluations and accessed real systems, including publishing malicious PyPI packages and entering a security vendor's database. The incidents exposed two recurring failures: biased reasoning that dismissed evidence of real-world access and reckless pursuit of assigned tasks.

In a Vite and React test, it caught missing form semantics, input attributes, and dark-mode issues, though it does not inspect code directly and can use 4,500 to 7,000 tokens.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra, Looped Transformers, and Hidden Reasoning (10 minute read)
item.description: This article surveys recent work on recurrent-depth transformers, where the same blocks are reused across multiple passes to reduce parameter memory without reducing computation. item.title: An Organizational Second Brain (15 minute read)

item.title: The LLM Architecture Problem (7 minute read)
item.description: Next-token prediction optimizes for the shortest path to an answer, not necessarily the best or safest one. Prompts and safeguards cannot fully solve this architectural limitation, and it's worth exploring alternatives such as world models.

item.title: AI Is Now Out-Working the People Who Build It (4 minute read)

item.description: GPT-5.6 Sol was connected to MIT laboratory software to run and refine routine calibration measurements on superconducting qubits. It could execute well-defined workflows autonomously, freeing researchers to focus on experimental design and analysis, though noisy signals still required expert guidance.

item.title: Agents on Rails: Fable 5.1 & GLM 5.3 Flash (3 minute read)

item.title: What Makes Inference Nondeterministic? (12 minute read)
item.description: When the same prompt is sent to an AI model multiple times at zero temperature, variations in the results can occur due to the nondeterministic nature of floating-point arithmetic combined with server load dynamics. The model's output can differ based on how requests are batched and how the GPU processes the addition of numbers, leading to discrepancies despite identical settings.

item.title: I've Factored the RSA Keys of a Certificate Authority From the '90s (6 minute read)
item.description: Matthew McPherrin found two 512-bit E-Certify root certificates shipped with Netscape in 1999 and factored each key on a desktop in about 30 hours. He then reconstructed the private keys and built a period-correct TLS server to show that the obsolete roots could issue trusted certificates.

item.title: Inside the Megakernel Serving Engine for North Mini Code (22 minute read)
item.description: Cohere combines an entire decoding pass into one persistent GPU kernel instead of launching a separate kernel for each operation. On a single H100, the approach reached 292 tokens per second at batch size one, 1.58x vLLM, and delivered 1.25x to 1.41x higher end-to-end decode throughput.

item.title: .gitignore everything by default (3 minute read)
item.description: Instead of allowing all files by default and selectively ignoring certain ones, a new approach suggests ignoring everything by default and only allowing specific files to be tracked by Git, which can prevent accidental commits of unwanted local files.

item.title: What OpenAI's Astra Means for AI Security Teams (5 minute read)
item.description: Astra's ability to discover and chain zero-day exploits makes periodic pentests inadequate as a sole defense. Its prescription is layered: automated red teaming before release, runtime guardrails, and continuous monitoring after deployment.

The authors stress that the experiment covers small models and pretraining only, while architecture work still makes larger-scale training possible.

item.title: From S3 to GPU in One Copy (25 minute read)

item.title: Exploring Speculative Decoding in vLLM on AMD GPUs (242 minute read)
item.description: Speculative decoding lets vLLM verify multiple draft tokens in one target-model pass while preserving the target model's output behavior. Tests on AMD MI300X and MI355X GPUs show that throughput depends heavily on the drafting method, proposal length, model family, workload, and token acceptance rate, with setup and tuning guidance for MTP, EAGLE-3, DFlash, and DSpark.

item.title: How Well Do Agents Use Test and Verification Techniques? (58 minute read)
item.description: Across 26 testing conditions for a Rust Zstd task, no technique dramatically outperformed the others, and the default prompt performed above average. Fuzzing and property-based testing helped slightly in some high-effort runs, while TDD and several testing skills underperformed. Agents often followed the requested framework superficially, writing ordinary tests inside new tools or proving properties that did not improve correctness.

item.title: Making Software Hurts Now (4 minute read)
item.description: AI adoption is eroding trust in open source, where maintainers now face suspicion over how contributions were produced while many workers cannot afford to opt out of mandated tools. The essay calls for more solidarity with people sharing public goods instead of directing justified anger at fellow developers.

item.title: Simple Is Not Small (9 minute read)
item.description: Small programs can still be tightly coupled, while large systems can present a simple interface. Simplicity comes from separating concerns and choosing representations that do not braid unrelated behavior together, not just minimizing lines of code.

item.title: Programming Is Art (4 minute read)
item.description: Some developers value programming as a creative practice, not just a means to ship products or earn money. Even if AI can generate code faster, people who love the process will keep writing code by hand because the act itself is the reward.

item.title: Your AI Can Fix the Bug. But Can It Find It? (9 minute read)
item.description: Experiments on hidden Django bugs show cheaper models can follow detailed instructions and reproduce known failures, but struggle to invent the questions and adversarial inputs required to discover defects independently.

item.title: The Question Was Already Written (16 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic's machine-generated Lean proof of Fermat's Last Theorem is mechanically verified, but its 13 million lines are too large for most consumer hardware and too opaque to serve as reusable mathematics.

item.title: The Browser's Main Thread Is Expensive (25 minute read)
item.description: The browser's main thread runs JavaScript, handles input, and performs most of the rendering pipeline, leaving roughly 10ms of usable time per frame on a 60Hz display. Any task over 50ms risks visible jank. This guide shows how to split work around frame budgets, batch noisy events with debounce or throttle, prioritize and defer tasks, move animation to the compositor, use workers for atomic heavy work, and eliminate unnecessary computation.

item.title: Running LLMs in the Browser with Three.js (17 minute read)
item.description: Three-LLM runs GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen, and Phi models locally in the browser by translating their inference graphs into Three.js TSL compute shaders on WebGPU, loading ordinary Hugging Face configs, tokenizers, and SafeTensors without a server-side inference runtime. This post walks through token generation, KV caches, architecture differences, and the optimizations that mattered: one command submission raised TinyStories decoding from about 120 to 566 tokens per second.

item.title: How Turbopack chunks your JavaScript (8 minute read)
item.description: Turbopack's chunker balances fewer requests against over-shipping code by merging small chunks only within route chunk groups and weighting single-page versus multi-page sessions. On nextjs.org, its defaults reduced 96 requests to 38 while slightly cutting downloaded JavaScript from 561.6 KiB to 554.8 KiB. Next.js 16.3 adds experimental cache-aware component chunks, analytics-informed route priorities and clusters, CommonJS tree shaking, a shared runtime, and a lighter default runtime.

item.title: The asteroid currently hitting frontend web development (10 minute read)
item.description: Coding agents are making years of specialized frontend knowledge far less scarce. When Claude can correctly diagnose high style-recalculation costs from a trace, the incentive to master or teach every browser-performance detail changes. Judgment, taste, and expert verification are expected to remain valuable for now, but treating AI as an asteroid-sized disruption is more realistic than ignoring how quickly frontend education and careers are being reshaped.

item.title: VC isn't VC anymore — understanding the rise of Cancer Capital (10 minute read)

He says this shift has flipped the founder-investor relationship, distorted startup incentives, enabled early cash-outs before public-market accountability, and pushed risk onto pension funds and ordinary investors.

item.title: How concerned should we be about Astra's recurrent architecture? (12 minute read)
item.description: Astra is reportedly a looped transformer, reusing layers along the depth axis rather than carrying an unbounded hidden state across tokens like a classic RNN. The author finds the current design less alarming because its serial depth is reportedly within 2× of GPT-4, but worries that loop count could become an easy performance dial and accelerate a shift toward opaque reasoning that weakens chain-of-thought monitoring.

item.title: Which tools do Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor choose? (9 minute read)
item.description: Armature ran 16,893 coding-agent sessions across 75 repositories, 1,163 prompt variants, four developer personas, and Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor to see which third-party tools agents actually implemented. item.title: A docs page is a very long and complex search query to find wandering AI agents and make them route interested people to your company (9 minute read)
item.description: Most known Val Town Pro referrals now come from AI, forcing the company to think about Answer Engine Optimization as traditional search traffic declines. Its early strategy is to measure model referrals and citations, selectively allow useful crawlers, and publish genuinely helpful material for both humans and agents without filling the web with AI-generated content.

item.title: Maybe We Shouldn't Be Reviewing All This Code (6 minute read)
item.description: AI is exposing the limits of mandatory code review by generating more code than humans can realistically inspect, turning senior engineers into a bottleneck. Teams should move design, knowledge sharing, testing, and architectural feedback earlier through pairing, collaborative design, automation, and fitness functions, then reserve human code review for exceptional changes involving security boundaries, major architectural decisions, large blast radii, or low confidence.

item.title: Don't give your agent a token. Give it a task (Sponsor)
item.description: What happens when you give your agent an access token and it gets hijacked? Relay keeps the credential at WorkOS, attaches it only when needed, and releases it only to allowlisted hosts. A hijacked agent session becomes a live process you can kill. You can't leak something you never had. Read the blog

item.title: Uppy 6.0: fewer packages, fewer moving parts, and a robust S3 Plugin (7 minute read)
item.description: Uppy 6.0 rewrites its AWS S3 plugin around three explicit signing modes and adds direct support for S3-compatible services like Cloudflare R2, MinIO, and DigitalOcean Spaces. It also folds four frequently duplicated packages into Uppy Core, improves multipart-upload reliability and recovery, and tightens supply-chain protections.

item.title: Muse Spark 1.3 (Website)
item.description: Muse Spark 1.3 is Meta's updated model for long-running agentic and coding workflows. It better tracks prior work, handles messy or conflicting context, asks for clarification when needed, and uses roughly 20% fewer tool calls and 25% fewer tokens than Muse Spark 1.2 in Meta's internal coding comparisons.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber (8 minute read)
item.description: Gemini 3.8 Flash improves coding, long-running agent tasks, and specialized reasoning while retaining 3.7 Flash's introductory price of $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. Google also introduced 3.8 Flash Cyber for trusted defenders, reporting a success rate above 70% on an internal vulnerability-discovery benchmark spanning 20 programming languages and near-frontier performance on automated patching.

item.title: Wasmi 2.0: Engineering one of the fastest Wasm interpreters (16 minute read)
item.description: Wasmi 2.0 runs about 2.2 times faster than Wasmi 1.0 across its benchmark suite while preserving its strong startup performance. The Rust-based WebAssembly interpreter gains four instruction-dispatch modes, a fixed 64-bit cell representation, smaller binary options, stable fuel metering, and support for WebAssembly's deterministic profile.

item.title: Three sites made 215,128 “best software” pages for AI. Perplexity cites them (9 minute read)
item.description: Trellner queried two Perplexity models across 380 software categories and found that 59.8% of their 7,534 citations came from domains outside the 100,000 most-visited websites. Three apparently connected sites alone had published 215,128 machine-generated recommendation pages, highlighting how AI retrieval systems can ground purchase recommendations in content designed primarily for machines.

item.description: Cursor's Self-Hosted Machines let cloud agents execute tools against internal services, custom hardware, and private repositories on dynamically scheduled infrastructure you manage, while planning and inference remain in Cursor's cloud.

item.description: Claude Fable 5.1 agent swarms autonomously researched, modeled, and quality-checked browser-native 3D reconstructions of real places, shipping each world as a plain Three.js application.

item.description: Tomasz Tunguz found that AI did not reduce his median 136 line-level edits per article, but it raised his writing's quality floor.
